palagiano.intro: Palagiano's tree is the Pino di Lenne, an Aleppo pine in the pinewood of Marina di Lenne on the Ionian coast, 4.45 metres round and 22 metres tall in Puglia's register of monumental trees. A national report on the dunes here calls it more than 600 years old. It stands about 20 metres from the road through the pines, inside the Stornara state nature reserve, and the beach in front of it carries its name.
palagiano.meta_description: The Pino di Lenne, a giant Aleppo pine in the Marina di Lenne pinewood near Palagiano, 4.45 m round: where it stands and how to find it.
palagiano.question_meta: The Pino di Lenne is a monumental Aleppo pine in the Marina di Lenne pinewood near Palagiano, about 20 metres from the road behind the beach.
palagiano.question_answer: The tree to see near Palagiano is the Pino di Lenne, an Aleppo pine 4.45 metres round and 22 metres tall in the pinewood behind the Lenne beach on the Ionian coast. A national report calls it more than 600 years old. It stands about 20 metres from the road through the pines and costs nothing to visit.
palagiano.question_context: Marina di Lenne is the coast of Palagiano on the Gulf of Taranto, about 7 kilometres from the town. Behind the beach a pinewood of Aleppo pine runs along the dunes, part of the Stornara state nature reserve, with juniper on the sand nearer the sea. Puglia's register of monumental trees lists one tree here, the Pino di Lenne, 4.45 metres round and 22 metres tall. A national report on restoring the dunes of Chiatona and Lenne calls it enormous and more than 600 years old, and says some consider it the oldest Aleppo pine in Europe; it does not say how the age was found. The beach in front of it is named after it. The tree stands about 20 metres from the road that runs through the pinewood, so a short walk from where you park is enough. No source sets out rules for walking in this part of the reserve, so keep to the tracks and off the dune plants. There is no public transport to the beach that we could find; by car or bike it is about 15 minutes from Palagiano.

faq.q: How old is the Pino di Lenne?
faq.a: A national report on the Lenne dunes calls it more than 600 years old and says some consider it the oldest Aleppo pine in Europe. It gives no basis for the figure, and nobody has dated the tree.

faq.q: How do you get to the Pino di Lenne?
faq.a: Drive or cycle from Palagiano to Marina di Lenne, about 7 kilometres. The tree stands in the pinewood behind the beach, about 20 metres from the road through the pines.

vico-del-gargano.intro: Vico del Gargano's tree is the holm oak in front of the Capuchin friary, 5.2 metres round and 18 metres tall in Puglia's register of monumental trees. A plaque says a friar planted it some 300 years ago. It stands in the open forecourt, ringed by a stone bench, a few minutes' walk from the old centre, and you do not need to enter the friary to see it.
vico-del-gargano.meta_description: The Capuchins' holm oak in Vico del Gargano, 5.2 m round and planted by a friar some 300 years ago by its plaque: where it stands and how to visit.
vico-del-gargano.question_meta: The holm oak of the Capuchins stands in the open forecourt of the friary in Vico del Gargano, a few minutes' walk from the old centre.
vico-del-gargano.question_answer: The tree to see in Vico del Gargano is the holm oak of the Capuchins, 5.2 metres round and 18 metres tall, in the open forecourt of the Capuchin friary. A plaque says a friar planted it some 300 years ago. It is free to see at any time, a few minutes on foot from the old centre.
vico-del-gargano.question_context: Vico del Gargano is a hill town in the north of the Gargano promontory, between the Foresta Umbra and the coast at San Menaio. Its best-known tree stands in front of the friary of the Santissimo Crocifisso, kept by Capuchin friars. Puglia's register of monumental trees gives the holm oak 5.2 metres round and 18 metres tall, and the State Forestry Corps classed it as a tree of exceptional historical and monumental value. A plaque says it was planted by a friar of the town, Fra' Nicola da Vico, some 300 years ago; that is the only date given for it. The botanist Adriano Fiori recorded it by the end of the nineteenth century. A storm in 1934 took one of its main branches and the trunk carries a long split. The tree stands in the open forecourt, ringed by a low stone bench, so the friary itself need not be entered. On Good Friday the confraternities stop in front of the friary on their procession. Buses run to Vico from Foggia and Peschici; there is no railway station in the town.

faq.q: Can you visit the holm oak of the Capuchins?
faq.a: Yes. It stands in the open forecourt in front of the Capuchin friary, free and open at all times, so you do not need to go inside the friary.

faq.q: How old is the Capuchins' holm oak in Vico del Gargano?
faq.a: A plaque at the friary says a friar planted it some 300 years ago. Nobody has dated the tree itself; the register gives it 5.2 metres round and 18 metres tall.

foresta-umbra.intro: The Foresta Umbra is the state forest at the centre of the Gargano promontory, and its tree to see is the Faggio dei Baracconi, a beech 5.2 metres round and 26 metres tall, one of five Puglia trees in the ministry's national book of monumental trees. It stands at Baracconi, where one of the forest's fifteen marked trails begins. The forest is free and open, with parking at the trailheads.
foresta-umbra.meta_description: The Faggio dei Baracconi, a 5.2 m beech in the Foresta Umbra on the Gargano, in Italy's national book of monumental trees: where it stands, how to visit.
foresta-umbra.question_meta: The Faggio dei Baracconi is a monumental beech in the Foresta Umbra, at Baracconi where trail 3 begins on the road from Villaggio Umbra towards Vieste.
foresta-umbra.question_answer: The tree to see in the Foresta Umbra is the Faggio dei Baracconi, a beech 5.2 metres round and 26 metres tall at Baracconi, where trail 3 begins on the road from Villaggio Umbra towards Vieste. It was one of five Puglia trees chosen for Italy's national book of monumental trees. The forest is free and open.
foresta-umbra.question_context: The Foresta Umbra covers the high centre of the Gargano promontory in northern Puglia, a state forest of beech, oak and maple inside the Gargano National Park, and its old beech stands are part of the UNESCO World Heritage listing of Europe's ancient beech forests. Puglia's register of monumental trees lists four beeches in it, and the two thickest are 5.2 metres round. One of them, at Baracconi, is the beech that went into the ministry's national book Alberi monumentali d'Italia in 2019 as one of five trees from Puglia; the register gives it 26 metres tall. Nobody has published its age. The forest has fifteen marked trails with parking at the trailheads, and trail 3 starts at Baracconi on the road from Villaggio Umbra towards Vieste. The register's group of old yews at Falascone stands in a fenced reserve kept for research, and only its fence line can be walked. There is no regular public transport into the forest; the road in runs from Vico del Gargano and Monte Sant'Angelo by way of Villaggio Umbra.

faq.q: Can you visit the old yews of the Foresta Umbra?
faq.a: Not up close. The register's yews at Falascone stand in a fenced reserve kept for research, and visitors can only walk along the fence. The Faggio dei Baracconi stands outside it, where trail 3 begins.

faq.q: How big is the Faggio dei Baracconi?
faq.a: Puglia's register of monumental trees gives it 5.2 metres round and 26 metres tall, level with the thickest beech it lists in the forest.

bisceglie.intro: Bisceglie's tree to see is a pistachio in the Giardino Botanico Santonio Veneziani, a small municipal garden in town. Puglia's register of monumental trees gives it a trunk 2.68 metres round, far thicker than a pistachio usually grows, and 7 metres tall. The garden has no regular opening hours: visits are booked with the association that runs it, and the guided ones have been free with a donation.
bisceglie.meta_description: A pistachio 2.68 m round in the Veneziani botanical garden in Bisceglie, on Puglia's list of monumental trees: how to book a visit to see it.
bisceglie.question_meta: The monumental pistachio of Bisceglie grows in the Giardino Botanico Santonio Veneziani, a small municipal garden open for booked visits.
bisceglie.question_answer: The tree to see in Bisceglie is the pistachio in the Giardino Botanico Santonio Veneziani, 2.68 metres round and 7 metres tall in Puglia's register of monumental trees, unusually thick for a pistachio. The garden has no regular opening hours, so book a visit with the association that runs it.
bisceglie.question_context: Bisceglie is a port town on the Adriatic between Trani and Molfetta, north of Bari. Puglia's register of monumental trees lists three trees in it: a holm oak on Corso Umberto I, a cypress in the Orto Schinosa, and a pistachio in the Giardino Botanico Santonio Veneziani. The pistachio is the surprise. Pistachio trees usually stay small, a few metres of twisting branches grown for their nuts, and the register gives this one a trunk 2.68 metres round and a height of 7 metres. The garden was left to the town by Colonel Santonio Veneziani and is looked after by the association Mosquito APS, which runs guided visits, school workshops, picnics and evening events there. It has no regular opening hours; visits are booked with the association, and the guided ones have been free with a donation. Nobody has published the tree's age. Bisceglie's railway station, on the line between Bari and Foggia, is about a kilometre from the garden.

faq.q: Can you visit the Veneziani botanical garden in Bisceglie?
faq.a: Yes, by booking. The garden has no regular opening hours; the association Mosquito APS runs booked visits, and its guided visits have been free with a donation.

faq.q: How big is the pistachio in Bisceglie?
faq.a: Puglia's register of monumental trees gives it a trunk 2.68 metres round and a height of 7 metres, far thicker than a pistachio usually grows.
